paragraphs: Choosing a reinforcement learning policy is difficult when historical interaction data are plentiful but new interactions are expensive or restricted. Off-policy evaluation estimates how candidate policies would perform using existing logs. The paper starts from the observation that these estimates can differ substantially from evaluations carried out in the actual environment.

The proposed approach combines the two sources of evidence in a sequential selection process. It first uses estimates from logged data to initialize online evaluation. It then uses Bayesian optimization to decide which policy should receive the next allocation of scarce environment interactions. A kernel represents similarities between policies, making those relationships part of the selection procedure.

Across multiple benchmarks with many candidate policies, the approach improves on both leading off-policy estimates and evaluation based purely on online interaction. The contribution is a way to direct a limited evaluation budget toward identifying the best policy, while making use of information already present in historical data.
neurips-2021-active-offline-policy-selec.tldr: Active offline policy selection combines logged-data estimates with strategically chosen online evaluations to select policies under a limited interaction budget.

paragraphs: A classifier trained on an uncurated dataset can perform poorly for groups that appear less often in its training examples. This paper addresses that problem through the construction of the training set itself. Its objective is minimax fairness: learning with attention to the group facing the worst classification performance.

The authors propose an adaptive sampling algorithm based on optimism and establish theoretical bounds on its performance. Sampling is therefore part of the learning strategy, rather than a fixed preliminary choice. They also develop heuristic extensions intended to make the approach usable for larger practical problems.

To assess what improvement is possible, the paper derives lower bounds that apply regardless of the algorithm for a particular class of problems. These show that the adaptive method's performance cannot generally be improved. Experiments with logistic regression on synthetic tasks and convolutional networks on real-world tasks support the benefits of adaptive dataset construction. Together, the results connect a fairness objective to both a sampling procedure and limits on achievable performance.
neurips-2021-adaptive-sampling-for-minim.tldr: Adaptive training-data sampling improves minimax fairness, with theoretical guarantees and supporting experiments.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks process data whose elements are connected by links, but choosing their architecture often requires substantial manual design. Automated graph neural networks search for suitable architectures. This paper identifies a weakness in existing approaches: their treatment of link information is largely implicit, which limits their suitability for predicting links and can also hinder other graph tasks.

AutoGEL makes link information an explicit part of the model. It also introduces a search space covering design choices both within individual layers and between layers. A differentiable search algorithm is used to explore these choices, with the aim of improving the efficiency and effectiveness of architecture selection.

The authors report superior benchmark performance across several tasks, including link prediction, node classification, and graph classification. The central contribution joins two decisions that affect graph learning: how connections are represented and how the network architecture is selected. Explicitly modeling links supports the prediction of connections while also improving the reported results for classifying nodes and whole graphs.
neurips-2021-autogel-an-automated-graph-.tldr: AutoGEL combines explicit link modeling with automated architecture search to improve several graph learning tasks.

paragraphs: Filter pruning compresses a neural network by removing filters and the computation associated with them. Many approaches judge a filter using information from its own channel. CHIP instead examines relationships between channels, asking how much independent information a feature map contributes relative to other feature maps.

The proposed Channel Independence measure captures these correlations. A feature map with low independence is interpreted as carrying less useful additional information, making its filter a candidate for removal. The paper investigates how to quantify and measure independence, as well as the sensitivity and reliability of the measure for pruning.

Experiments show that substantial compression can accompany small accuracy improvements in the evaluated models. On CIFAR-10, the reported ResNet-56 result reduces model size by 42.8% and FLOPs by 47.4%, with a 0.75% accuracy increase. On ImageNet, ResNet-50 achieves 40.8% less storage and 44.8% less computation, with a 0.15% accuracy increase. These findings support using redundancy between channels as a practical guide for deciding which filters to remove.
neurips-2021-chip-channel-independence-b.tldr: CHIP prunes filters using correlations between feature maps, achieving substantial compression with small accuracy gains in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Models with discrete latent variables require gradient estimates that can be highly variable, making training difficult. Replacing discrete variables with a continuous approximation can help, but such a relaxation is not always available or practical. The paper builds on an estimator that avoids continuous relaxation but previously applied only to binary variables.

The authors derive that estimator through importance sampling and statistical coupling, then extend the construction to categorical variables with more than two possible values. They also develop estimators that express a categorical variable as a sequence of binary choices. A stick-breaking coupling motivates this construction, while Rao-Blackwellization provides an additional way to reduce variability in estimation.

Systematic experiments show state-of-the-art performance for the proposed categorical estimators. The comparisons also reveal that some previous estimators remain worse than a simpler REINFORCE estimator with a leave-one-out baseline, even after additional Rao-Blackwellization. The findings support the specific coupling-based constructions and show why more elaborate variance-reduction machinery does not automatically yield better empirical performance.
neurips-2021-coupled-gradient-estimators.tldr: The paper extends coupling-based gradient estimation from binary to categorical latent variables and reports strong empirical performance.

paragraphs: Models of human behavior often describe people collectively, while useful interaction with individuals may require understanding differences between them. This paper studies behavioral stylometry: identifying a person from the decisions they make. Chess provides the setting, with the task of determining which player produced a set of games.

The authors develop a transformer-based approach within a few-shot classification framework. The method learns representations of playing behavior that can distinguish individual players. It identifies a player among thousands of candidates with 98% accuracy given 100 labeled games, demonstrating a strong identification signal in the decisions contained in those games.

A model trained on amateur play also generalizes to Grandmaster samples outside its training distribution, despite the substantial difference in playing strength. The authors examine what the resulting embeddings reveal about individual chess styles and discuss ethical implications of identifying people from behavior. The reported transfer suggests that the learned distinctions are useful beyond the amateur population on which the method was trained.
neurips-2021-detecting-individual-decisi.tldr: A transformer identifies chess players from their decisions with high reported accuracy and transfers from amateur to Grandmaster play.

paragraphs: Learning many tasks without supervision requires an agent to find worthwhile goals and learn how to reach them. LEXA separates these responsibilities between an explorer and an achiever. Both learn through imagined trajectories generated by a world model trained from images, allowing the agent to practice using its learned account of the environment.

The explorer uses foresight to seek surprising states that have not yet been visited. Those discoveries become diverse targets for the achiever. This gives goal discovery and goal practice distinct roles: exploration expands the collection of targets, while the achiever learns to reliably reach them.

After unsupervised training, LEXA can attempt tasks specified by goal images without further learning. The authors report substantial improvements over previous unsupervised goal-reaching approaches on existing benchmarks and a new benchmark containing 40 tasks across four robotic manipulation and locomotion domains. They also report success on goals requiring sequential interaction with multiple objects. These findings show that the learned abilities can support both varied targets and goals involving several interactions.
neurips-2021-discovering-and-achieving-g.tldr: LEXA learns to discover and achieve diverse visual goals through world-model imagination, then tackles goal-image tasks without additional learning.

paragraphs: Imitation learning seeks a policy from expert demonstrations when the reward function is unavailable. A difficulty is that demonstrated behavior may be noisy or inconsistently optimal. This paper studies a distributionally robust formulation that uses an adversarial construction to guard against overly optimistic conclusions from the demonstrations.

The analysis connects distributionally robust imitation learning with maximum entropy inverse reinforcement learning. In this view, the robust objective maximizes a generalized form of entropy. For a class of losses that add contributions over states and actions, the authors transform the objective into a convex optimization problem with a polynomial number of variables.

The resulting method can optimize both stationary policies and policies that change over time. It also avoids repeatedly solving an inner reinforcement learning problem, a requirement of prevalent earlier approaches. Experiments on synthetic data and a highway driving environment show significant benefits from the new optimization method. The contribution combines a robustness-based account of imperfect demonstrations with a tractable optimization formulation for the stated class of losses.
neurips-2021-distributionally-robust-imi.tldr: Distributionally robust imitation learning connects generalized entropy with a convex formulation for learning from imperfect demonstrations.

paragraphs: Policy updates focused on states visited by the current policy can leave other states insufficiently considered, contributing to convergence on a suboptimal policy. This paper extends policy gradient theory to updates defined using arbitrary state distributions. It establishes a necessary and sufficient condition on those distributions for convergence to optimality under the generalized updates.

The analysis also gives improved asymptotic convergence rates. To put its principles into practice, the authors introduce an agent with two independent policies: Dr Jekyll exploits current knowledge, while Mr Hyde explores. Their experience is stored in separate replay buffers, enabling a mixture of on-policy and off-policy updates.

Experiments on finite Markov decision processes show stronger recovery from convergence toward suboptimal policies without slowing convergence. A deep version produces promising results on a simple problem. The broader contribution is a set of principles for actor-critic methods: exploration and exploitation can generate distinct experience sources, and their use in updates should meet the state-distribution requirements identified by the theory.
neurips-2021-dr-jekyll-mr-hyde-the-stran.tldr: Generalized policy-update theory motivates separate exploring and exploiting policies that help an agent recover from suboptimal behavior.

paragraphs: Collaborative medical-image training can use data held at different hospitals without gathering patient images in one place. Federated learning supports this arrangement by exchanging network weights, but large models can impose substantial communication costs. Split learning divides a model between clients and a server, creating a related challenge: choosing a division that preserves performance.

The paper combines these approaches using a Vision Transformer. Its readily decomposable architecture provides a basis for separating client and server computation while retaining model performance. The framework is evaluated using chest X-ray datasets from multiple sources, including uneven data distributions intended to resemble collaboration between hospitals.

In those experiments, the framework achieves performance comparable to centralized training. It also improves individual task performance, including COVID-19 diagnosis, when participating clients have different tasks, while avoiding the exchange of large parameter sets. The findings support the suitability of Transformers for this form of collaborative medical-image learning and provide evidence for the proposed architecture under heterogeneous data and task conditions.
neurips-2021-federated-split-task-agnost.tldr: A federated split Vision Transformer supports collaborative chest X-ray learning with reduced weight-sharing demands and performance comparable to centralized training.

paragraphs: Generalization bounds aim to describe how learning performance carries beyond the training data. This paper develops information-theoretic bounds for supervised learning by changing which information is measured. It focuses on the information contained in predictions, rather than the information in the output produced by the training algorithm.

That choice addresses two practical obstacles in earlier information-theoretic analyses. The new bounds provide meaningful results for deterministic algorithms, and they are substantially easier to estimate. The authors also establish improvements over existing bounds and applicability to a broader range of learning algorithms. Thus, the contribution concerns both the scope of the theory and how readily its quantities can be assessed.

Experiments in practical deep-learning settings show that the proposed bounds closely track the generalization gap. This empirical finding connects the theoretical quantities to observed differences in generalization behavior. The paper's central message is that predictions can provide a useful basis for analyzing generalization, with advantages for deterministic learning procedures and practical estimation.
neurips-2021-information-theoretic-gener.tldr: Prediction-based information bounds broaden generalization analysis, handle deterministic algorithms, and closely track observed deep-learning generalization gaps.

paragraphs: Few-shot learning commonly organizes training into small episodes, each containing its own training and validation subsets. This arrangement imitates evaluation, where a model must classify examples using little labeled data. The paper asks whether imposing this structure is useful for methods that make predictions through nonparametric comparisons within each episode.

The authors investigate Matching Networks and Prototypical Networks through extensive ablation experiments. For these methods, they show that episodic constraints are unnecessary and can use the examples in a training batch inefficiently. Their non-episodic counterparts remove those constraints, producing simpler training approaches with fewer hyperparameters.

The non-episodic versions improve performance across multiple few-shot classification datasets. These findings challenge the assumption that training must mirror the episode structure of evaluation for the investigated class of methods. The practical significance is that simplifying the training organization can improve how available examples are used while also improving measured classification performance. The conclusion is specifically grounded in methods using nonparametric prediction at the episode level.
neurips-2021-on-episodes-prototypical-ne.tldr: For the studied nonparametric few-shot methods, removing episodic training constraints simplifies learning and improves data use and classification performance.

paragraphs: Real-world networks often contain many triangles and other recurring small structures. This paper asks why graph generators can struggle to reproduce those patterns, even when they use sophisticated neural networks. It studies models that generate each edge independently according to an assigned probability, a family encompassing both classical and modern approaches.

The authors prove limits on the triangle and other subgraph densities these models can produce under a bounded-overlap condition. That condition prevents a model from simply memorizing a single graph. The qualification matters: the theorem concerns independent-edge generation while restricting the extent to which generated graphs can overlap.

The paper also introduces a simple generator that balances overlap against reconstruction accuracy. It performs comparably to more complex models on many graph statistics. Together, the theoretical and empirical results identify a structural tradeoff in this model family. More elaborate model machinery does not remove the proved restriction when edge independence and bounded overlap remain in place, while a simple model can still reproduce many measured properties effectively.
neurips-2021-on-the-power-of-edge-indepe.tldr: Under bounded overlap, independent-edge graph generators face provable limits in reproducing dense triangles and other subgraphs.

paragraphs: Estimating a discrete distribution becomes harder when observations must be communicated using a limited number of bits. Many analyses describe the worst case across all distributions. This paper instead gives pointwise bounds, so the estimation error reflects the particular distribution being estimated rather than only the number of possible outcomes.

For sufficiently many samples, the upper bound is governed by the distribution's half-norm and the communication budget, together with a term inversely proportional to sample size. The authors achieve this rate with a two-round interactive procedure. The first round obtains a coarse estimate using a global method; the remaining samples refine that estimate locally.

An almost matching local lower bound shows limits that apply to any interactive scheme. Its proof uses a parametric model containing the target distribution and bounds the information retained after quantization. Together, the bounds indicate that a Rényi-entropy quantity characterizes the local communication needed to match centralized performance under the stated loss. This links communication difficulty to distribution-specific structure rather than ambient dimension alone.
neurips-2021-pointwise-bounds-for-distri.tldr: Distribution-specific bounds show how local structure governs estimation accuracy and communication needs under a limited bit budget.

paragraphs: Vector graphics describe images through analytic primitives and their organization. This representation supports scaling without the aliasing or information loss associated with rasterization and supplies structural information about how elements form larger shapes. The paper explores how object recognition can use that information directly.

The proposed YOLaT pipeline reads the textual vector-graphics document without rendering it into pixels. It builds multiple graphs to represent spatial relationships and structural information, then uses a dual-stream graph neural network to locate and classify objects. The pipeline does not use a convolutional neural network, placing the vector document's relationships at the center of recognition.

Experiments show better average precision and efficiency than the evaluated object-detection baselines operating on raster graphics. The results support the value of preserving the original representation during recognition. In this setting, the vector document provides more than instructions for drawing an image: its organization supplies information that the graph-based detector can use for identifying objects and determining where they are.
neurips-2021-recognizing-vector-graphics.tldr: YOLaT detects objects directly from vector-graphics documents using graph networks, improving reported precision and efficiency over raster-based baselines.

paragraphs: In a latent Markov decision process, an environment is randomly selected from several possible environments, but the agent is not told which one was chosen. The paper studies how efficiently an agent can learn in this setting. It first proves that general instances may require a number of episodes exponential in the number of possible environments, even to approximate an optimal policy.

The authors then identify sufficient assumptions that permit learning with polynomially many episodes. A central requirement is adequate separation between the environments' dynamics. Under sufficient separation, their efficient algorithm has a local guarantee: it achieves sublinear regret when supplied with a good initialization.

The initialization requirement can be removed when additional statistical sufficiency assumptions from predictive state representations and a reachability assumption hold. These results distinguish the difficulty of unrestricted latent environments from cases where their structure supports efficient learning. The positive guarantees depend on the stated assumptions; separation is presented as a key sufficient ingredient, with further conditions enabling learning without the favorable starting point.
neurips-2021-rl-for-latent-mdps-regret-g.tldr: Latent MDPs can be exponentially hard to learn, but sufficient structural assumptions enable efficient algorithms with conditional regret guarantees.

paragraphs: Online linear regression makes predictions as data arrive over time. This paper studies the stochastic setting and compares online ridge regression with the forward algorithm through high-probability regret bounds. Regret measures the cumulative cost of the learner's predictions relative to a comparison predictor, making the bounds a way to assess learning performance over time.

The analysis removes assumptions that observations and predictions are bounded. It also gives a more precise comparison between the two algorithms. The authors advocate the forward algorithm because of its stronger bounds and robustness to the choice of regularization parameter, connecting the theoretical comparison to a practical algorithm-selection issue.

The paper further explains how to incorporate the forward algorithm into methods that use linear function approximation. This substitution can remove a boundedness assumption without worsening theoretical bounds. In linear bandit applications, the modification yields improved regret guarantees. Numerical experiments illustrate the analysis and support the authors' intuitions, complementing the theoretical argument for using the forward algorithm in the studied settings.
neurips-2021-stochastic-online-linear-re.tldr: New stochastic regret bounds favor the forward algorithm over online ridge regression and support improvements in linear bandit methods.

paragraphs: Training LSTM networks is expensive because hidden-state computation repeats across sequence positions. Their activation functions offer limited opportunities to exploit the kinds of naturally occurring zeros useful in some other networks. This paper instead uses sparsity created by dropout, which already removes neuron values during training for regularization.

The method coordinates dropout so that the same physical neurons are dropped across a batch. This produces entire rows or columns of sparsity, making the omitted work easier to exploit on SIMD hardware and systolic arrays. The authors analyze how this structure propagates through training and where it can reduce computation.

The approach is designed to replace dropout in existing application settings. Experiments cover language modeling, machine translation, and named entity recognition. Reported training speedups range from 1.23 to 1.64 times without sacrificing the target metric. The contribution is therefore both statistical and computational in its design: it retains a dropout-based training arrangement while organizing the missing values into patterns that hardware can use to reduce runtime.
neurips-2021-structured-in-space-randomi.tldr: Structuring dropout across batches turns LSTM sparsity into reported training speedups of 1.23–1.64 times without sacrificing task metrics.

paragraphs: Separating a reflection from a single image requires recovering two layers from one mixed observation: the transmitted scene and the reflection. The problem is highly ill-posed. Existing deep-learning approaches often reconstruct the layers largely independently, leaving limited interaction between the two processing branches until late in the network.

The proposed YTMT strategy makes the branches communicate at each block. It draws on the additive relationship between the two components: information that is unhelpful for reconstructing one layer may still help reconstruct the other. Specifically, information deactivated by a ReLU operation is transferred to the other stream instead of being discarded.

Ablation studies and experiments on commonly used reflection-separation datasets demonstrate the strategy's effectiveness and superiority over the compared state-of-the-art alternatives. The contribution is a simple way to make dual-stream decomposition use intermediate information more efficiently. By exchanging information throughout processing, the two branches participate in a connected reconstruction procedure rather than relying mainly on separate estimates or late interaction.
neurips-2021-trash-or-treasure-an-intera.tldr: YTMT improves reflection separation by transferring ReLU-deactivated information between the branches reconstructing transmission and reflection.

paragraphs: Speech contains structure at several timescales, from phonemes to words, with durations that vary by context. This paper investigates how speech-recognition networks combine information across time. It adapts temporal context invariance, a method from biological neuroscience, by comparing responses to the same segments placed in different surrounding contexts.

The method estimates the shortest segment duration needed for a response to become insensitive to its surroundings. In DeepSpeech2, nearly all units have compact integration windows, including units in recurrent layers. Training shortens those windows in early layers and lengthens them in higher layers, producing a hierarchy of temporal integration.

Tests with stretched and compressed speech reveal a transition around the middle of the trained network. Later integration windows follow the duration of speech structures more closely, while earlier windows track absolute time. Similar patterns appear in purely recurrent and purely convolutional networks, with stronger structure-linked integration in the recurrent model. These observations suggest a shared organizational pattern and provide a practical method for examining temporal processing inside otherwise opaque models.
neurips-2021-understanding-adaptive-mult.tldr: Context-based measurements reveal that trained speech networks progress from short time-based integration windows to longer windows aligned with speech structure.

paragraphs: Early stopping is often used when training labels contain errors, drawing on how deep networks memorize data during training. Usually, one stopping point is chosen for the whole network. This paper finds that layers respond differently to label noise: later layers are much more sensitive, while earlier layers are comparatively robust.

Progressive early stopping uses that difference to organize training in stages. Earlier layers receive relatively many training epochs. Later layers are then trained progressively for fewer epochs while preceding layers remain fixed. This gives the different parts of the network different amounts of training exposure instead of requiring one stopping decision to serve them all.

The authors report that the method can produce better and more stable results than traditional early stopping. Combined with existing methods for learning from noisy labels, it achieves state-of-the-art performance on image-classification benchmarks. The findings connect a layer-level observation about noise sensitivity to a simple training procedure, showing why treating the network as a single unit can be an unhelpful constraint.
neurips-2021-understanding-and-improving.tldr: Progressive early stopping trains noise-sensitive later layers for fewer epochs while giving more robust earlier layers longer training.

paragraphs: In a bandit problem with graph feedback, choosing an action can reveal information about other actions according to a directed graph. The paper asks how this observation structure determines minimax regret. Its aim is to characterize learning difficulty through graph properties that capture both achievable performance and unavoidable error.

The authors introduce fractional weak domination and a packing-based independence quantity. These correspond to a linear program for weak domination and its dual packing problem. Strong duality connects the two descriptions, supporting upper and lower regret bounds with the same two-thirds power dependence on the number of rounds.

The remaining difference between the bounds depends on a logarithmic factor and the dual problem's integrality gap. For graphs with bounded integrality gap, including trees and bounded-degree graphs, the bounds match up to the cube root of a logarithmic factor in the number of actions. For several special graph families, that factor can also be removed. The results make the observation graph's role explicit and identify cases where the optimal regret can be established.
neurips-2021-understanding-bandits-with-.tldr: Linked graph domination and packing quantities yield nearly matching regret bounds for bandits with graph feedback.

paragraphs: Advances in unsupervised visual learning have benefited large networks more than small ones. This paper proposes a single training phase that combines self-supervised learning with knowledge distillation. A teacher learns visual representations while a smaller student simultaneously learns to reproduce the teacher's predictions.

The teacher is trained to assign different views of the same image consistently to clusters. Because the teacher is still learning, its guidance is generated on the fly. The framework also uses a domain-classifier idea to guide the student with discriminative features that withstand differences between teacher and student representation spaces. Network-driven generation of multiple views supplies further feature information.

Experiments show that the students outperform the compared offline-distilled networks, including ones using stronger teachers, and leading self-supervised models. A ResNet-18 student trained with a ResNet-50 teacher reaches 68.3% ImageNet top-1 accuracy when a linear classifier evaluates its frozen features, 1.5% below the supervised baseline. This result supports simultaneous representation learning and transfer as an effective approach for the evaluated small networks.
neurips-2021-unsupervised-representation.tldr: Simultaneous self-supervised teacher training and distillation produce strong visual representations in small student networks.

paragraphs: Conventional meta-learning assumes tasks come from a stable distribution. This paper considers tasks arriving sequentially from a changing distribution, where transferring earlier knowledge can be unhelpful and learning new tasks can erase useful old knowledge. VC-BML addresses both issues through a Bayesian representation of the meta-parameters.

The method maintains a dynamic Gaussian mixture, with a Chinese Restaurant Process determining the number of components. Multiple components enlarge the parameter space available for adapting to diverse tasks, helping reduce negative knowledge transfer. The model can therefore represent task diversity through a changing mixture rather than a single fixed parameter estimate.

To infer parameter posteriors, the authors introduce structured variational inference as a more robust alternative to point estimation, with the aim of preserving knowledge. Experiments on tasks from non-stationary distributions show better transfer across diverse tasks and reduced catastrophic forgetting. The contribution combines a flexible representation of meta-parameters with posterior approximation, addressing both adaptation to changing tasks and retention of knowledge in the online setting.
neurips-2021-variational-continual-bayes.tldr: VC-BML uses dynamic Bayesian mixtures and structured variational inference to improve transfer and reduce forgetting across changing task distributions.

paragraphs: Visual information can enrich language learning with knowledge that text descriptions alone may not supply. VidLanKD transfers knowledge from video-language learning into a language model. The approach addresses limitations of supervision based on a finite set of retrieved image labels, including approximation error and restricted vocabulary diversity.

A multimodal teacher is trained on paired video and text. Its knowledge is then distilled into a student language model using a text dataset. The proposed distillation objectives are designed to avoid the approximation error associated with image-label supervision, while a large video-text dataset supports learning a richer and more varied vocabulary.

Experiments report consistent improvements over text-only and vokenization models on GLUE, SQuAD, and SWAG. Evaluations on additional datasets show improvements in world knowledge, physical reasoning, and temporal reasoning. Ablation studies and grounding visualizations further examine the approach. The findings support a two-stage route from visual experience to language understanding: learning from video and text jointly, then transferring that knowledge through text-based student training.
neurips-2021-vidlankd-improving-language.tldr: VidLanKD distills a video-language teacher into a text-trained student, improving reported language understanding and reasoning performance.
